published_building_trio_2026_09_06.placement: native houses repeat in plots; civic landmark stays fixed

quality_target: At least the user-approved Classic Haussmann level of archetype-shaped geometry, real construction depth, photoreal material response and resilient LEGO scaling in a real-time City Prompt GLB
purpose: Preserve the construction knowledge learned during the high-fidelity LEGO pilots and make it executable for catalogue-scale batches.

pillars.archetype_shape: Distinctive corners, courts, setbacks, roof profile and identity-bearing masses must form the archetype silhouette instead of decorating a generic box.
pillars.physical_depth: Open railings, balcony slabs, recesses, returns, cornices, dormers, entrances and other shadow-casting construction must project or recede at believable metric depth.
pillars.photoreal_skin: An archetype-specific render-locked PBR skin, layered glazing and occupied depth must remain convincing in the live City Prompt lighting stack.
pillars.lego_scalability: Fixed identity anchors retain authored proportions while complete repeatable middle bays and an authored fallback absorb ordinary user-drawn variation.

non_negotiable_principles.rule: Use every compatible archetype view to infer massing, corners, roof, entrances and side elevations; never optimize only for the card image.
Silhouette-changing and shadow-casting features are geometry. A facade photograph must not be asked to hide generic massing.

Every new or materially revised family must meet or exceed the user-approved Classic Haussmann goalpost in four dimensions together: archetype-shaped massing, real projecting/recessed/open construction, photoreal reference-locked materials and glazing, and LEGO scaling that preserves fixed identity while repeating complete middle bays.

A sculptural shell is one continuous plan-and-section envelope across front, sides and rear. Its exposed top, fascia and underside or soffit are separate semantic surfaces with deliberate thickness and materials; disconnected facade ribbons or one material on every face are prohibited.
Keep corner, entrance, podium, crown and roof assemblies fixed. Repeat or stretch only authored middle bays.

A stoop entrance, arched lobby or courtyard passage is a sectional void through the podium envelope, not a window image or bright object attached to the facade. Split or cut the wall and skin at the opening, preserve an unobstructed path, and construct jambs, soffit or ceiling, threshold, landing and circulation as one fixed assembly.

Reference-defining balcony and loggia stacks use one coordinated representation: physical slab, recessed back wall or opening, side returns, open rails and believable supports aligned to floor datums. Do not leave a second photographed balcony layer in the facade atlas beneath the physical assembly.

A fixed-landmark manifest declares a conservative fixedLandmarkScaleBand around native width and depth plus a maximum independent-axis ratio. Slight user-drawn footprint variation may use that authored band; a bounded uniform contain-fit may absorb a modestly smaller or differently proportioned site without deforming the landmark; larger or strongly elongated targets must use the stack kit, streetwall repetition or explicitly labelled forced fit.
Close-range facades use shadow-neutral albedo plus normal, roughness, AO/depth and emissive channels. City lighting remains the lighting authority.

A manifest channel declaration is not evidence of a textured model. The assessor resolves every near/far PBR atlas, semantic mask, render-locked source and skin manifest on disk, verifies declared widths, and the exported GLB must embed the registered materials.

Generic tiled facade materials are not a production skin. Every new archetype uses its compatible reference views to author a render-locked, archetype-specific source; registers that source by elevation and semantic surface; binds depth or displacement in the runtime shader; and forbids generic tiling as the primary identity treatment.

Treat image generation as a reproducible design-source stage. Retain compatible inputs, a labelled goalpost, immutable keeper outputs, exact prompts, provider and model, output roles and geometry-registration targets in the family source package so no approved method depends on chat history or temporary files.

A generated elevation, material study or occupied-depth source counts only when exported geometry actually references it. Coordinate-register the source to audited model datums, keep exterior screens and mullions as separate physical construction, and place reference-derived occupied depth immediately behind the matching physical glazing.

Keep the full render-locked elevation as the identity and registration authority, but do not stretch its photographed openings, shadows or perspective over long beams, curved shells, arch soffits or domes. Those physical solids use shadow-neutral tile-safe construction zones derived from the same reference palette; reference-specific occupation is clipped and coordinate-registered per real opening behind physical glazing.

Never repeat an oblique photograph crop across brick, ribbed metal, timber, concrete, roof, railing or service solids. Repeating construction skins come from orthographic shadow-neutral plates derived from the approved reference palette; perspective sources remain coordinate-registered elevations, special enclosures or occupied-depth cards.

Reference railings, pergolas and lightweight furniture are constructed from real posts, rails, balusters, beams, fins, seats, backs and legs. An opaque photograph-wrapped slab is not an acceptable substitute for a visually open assembly.

Preserve named semantic material zones while reusing identical approved construction-image paths and far LODs for secondary equipment. Delivery optimization may deduplicate embedded images but may not replace custom skins, drop required channels or collapse distinct optical and construction metadata.

The exported GLB keeps its authored physical transmission profile. A renderer-specific alpha-only glazing override is allowed only after export for locked-camera proof images, must be restored afterward, and may never alter the delivered optical material.

A crystalline, diagrid or polygonal facade must reconstruct the reference panel graph, documented shape families, physical scale and opaque-to-glazed ratio on the actual envelope. Clip boundary panels to curved voids and expose construction joints between opaque neighbours; a rectangular grid split into decorative triangles is not equivalent.

Use recessed panes, frame depth, registered physical mullions/transoms, interior backplates and occupied warm interiors. Use physical transmission near and baked facade glass far; an audited atlas may supply fine sash colour but not all close-range construction depth.

Share layered window construction, not one generic optical material. Match tint, roughness, coating, transmission, frame depth and occupation pattern to each archetype; keep panes nearly non-emissive, put warmth on recessed room cards, and avoid repeated blue/warm checkerboards.

Dormers, oriels, lanterns and gable windows use the same two-layer contract as facade openings: a physically shaded pane in front of a recessed occupied room card. A single opaque warm pane cannot provide reflections, parallax and interior depth at once.

Semantic glazing masks must follow the actual glass field: pointed and segmental arches, roundels and tracery groups may not be approximated by rectangular bounding boxes. The mask controls both the facade cut-out and the physical pane, so its silhouette is construction geometry at hero range.

Every near-range glazing assembly owns an unobstructed service cavity from exterior skin to occupied backplate. Structural massing cores must be inset far enough that panes and room cards never intersect or disappear behind the core.

A full-height lobby, station portal or market entrance is a sectional assembly: shaped opening, deep jambs and soffit, physical pane and frame, recessed dark backplane, and sparse local occupation lighting. A uniformly bright card behind an entire monumental glass field is prohibited because it flattens the cavity into a glowing texture.

Markets, stations and halls with multiple roof aisles or vaults must author every visible aisle, ridge, valley, clerestory, rib or truss family, and end fan. A single generic shell may not stand in for the reference roof system.

A detached house is a complete roof, threshold, privacy and occupation composition rather than a small generic stack. Its fixed whole-house assembly owns roof silhouette, entrance or porch, balconies or screens, chimneys or towers and residential-scale window construction; its repeatable fallback varies complete ordinary bays without duplicating those identity anchors.

Author front, left, right and rear elevations for every asset, including courtyard walls. Material courses, cornices, balconies, window returns and roof logic continue around exposed sides and corners; secondary elevations remain stylistically related but use a believable different opening and service hierarchy. Detail may be occluded only when site geometry confirms a true party wall.
Roofs, dormers, canopies, columns and other fixed assemblies inherit the archetype's material palette, edge profiles and construction logic; no attachment may introduce a separate visual language.
A family is not production-ready until it works at recommended small and large sizes and on every declared footprint profile.

Declare only footprint profiles that preserve the building's identity. A family may lower its required preferred-profile count only with an explicit minimumPreferredProfiles value and a non-empty profileRationale, then must prove in-band and oversized streetwall plans.

Manifest native width and depth define a placement and matching envelope, not a requirement to extrude every module across it. Preserve archetype-shaped occupied solids, setbacks, shoulders, voids and roof volumes inside that envelope, mark modules allow_inset_footprint, and apply one uniform horizontal contain scale to the complete landmark or stack at runtime instead of independently stretching axes or levels to the parcel edges.

Every placed building with a valid LEGO recipe resolves to its authored GLB in the normal site view. Admit every distinct family inside the supported total-stack budget; never leave later families as persistent generic grey massing proxies merely because a mixed plan uses more than two archetypes.

A building with a saved renderable LEGO recipe suppresses its planning prism and outline independently of transient asset-loader state. Clip several disjoint replacement footprints with one true world-coordinate polygon union and do not mount projected stencil volumes behind the authored GLBs; the normal 3D view must contain no pale blue, grey or white polygon boxes around them.
A selected variant manifest declares both the parent catalogue archetype id and selected variant id in archetype_aliases. Do not broaden aliases to materially different sibling aesthetics.

Compare archetype and model at block, building and facade scales using a street/front view, front-corner oblique, rear-corner oblique, high oblique/aerial, close facade and context view. No family is production-ready from one hero angle.

Generate a photoreal City Prompt render from each authoritative live camera and treat it as a construction goal post. The prompt must preserve the exact footprint, massing, height, roofline, silhouette, window rhythm and camera; it may improve materials, lighting and entourage but must not redesign the building. Compare the unchanged live 3D camera back to that image after every keeper iteration.
A materially or geometrically distinct catalogue variant owns its signature profile, reference provenance, physical atlas span and fixed massing assemblies; never inherit the parent family blindly.

The selected catalogue variant must rewrite generationStyleInput, image provenance and generation identifier before family export. Validate the resolved UI id and source thumbnail so sibling variants can never silently compile as variant_0.

Measure the user's drawn geographic polygon for every assembly. Catalogue dimensions guide suitability, but a native named tier should be authored when the real parcel would otherwise require excessive scaling.

Clip source tiles in world coordinates for every supported replacement footprint so photogrammetry behind the proposal remains visible. Several disjoint footprints share one polygon-union shader mask; projected stencil silhouettes are not acceptable in close orbit or render captures.

Choose and construct the load-bearing and enclosure grammar demanded by the archetype: continuous terra-cotta piers and setbacks, timber post-and-beam plus lattice, a freestanding steel curtain-wall grid, a transparent transit concourse under timber floors, or a deep passive-house rainscreen. Do not force unrelated families through one generic facade scaffold.

A catalogue sibling variant owns its own multi-angle goalpost, silhouette, structural grammar, entrance, roof topology, material zones, glazing profile, metric landmark and repeatable fallback kit. A parent-family recolour or reused assembled GLB is prohibited; variant ids and aesthetic aliases must resolve to the independently authored family.

Lock the ridge direction, eave hierarchy, overhang, slope and public versus rear roof fields against both front and aerial goalposts before detailing. Photovoltaic, sedum, tile, rooflight and canopy fields are separate physical assemblies clearly proud of their carrier planes.

Koshi lattice, timber louvers and exterior blinds remain real open geometry with screen-space gaps, a deliberate air cavity, physically shaded glass and occupied depth behind. A textured opaque panel or a screen fused to its pane is not equivalent.

When photovoltaics, sedum, rooflights, exterior blinds or planted roofs define the reference, construct their coverage, support, drainage edge and attachment relationship at true metric scale and preserve them in assembled and modular roof contracts.

A highly transparent curtain wall reveals one coherent interior volume across adjacent panes. Keep glass, pressure caps, floor and ceiling returns physical and use sparse modeled occupation; never repeat the same opaque room card immediately behind every pane.

A passive-house window is recessed behind the insulation line with complete jamb, head and sill returns, separate low-E glazing, external blind hardware and varied deep room shadow or occupation. A shallow pane or repeated room photograph is not equivalent.

A reference-defining photovoltaic field consists of standard-scale modules with one complete countable cell topology per module, individual perimeter frames, real inter-module gaps, mounting rails and roof-edge clearance; one stretched PV texture across a roof is prohibited.

When circulation, long-span structure or industrial transfer equipment defines an archetype, construct it as one continuous usable or load-bearing system with credible landings, supports, clearances and endpoints. A ski path, concourse nave, cable roof, silo gallery or public stair cannot be reduced to disconnected decorative pieces.

instructions: Reject or quarantine reference views that depict a different variant.
Record invariant cues shared by the views before writing geometry.
For one-view archetypes, lower confidence and require visual review.

image_generation.purpose: Create reproducible, render-locked design sources that preserve the selected archetype while supplying registered identity, material and occupied-depth evidence for the physical LEGO model.
prompt_contract: Name the exact catalogue archetype and selected variant and use only compatible saved inputs.
Declare one output role and its camera or projection; do not ask one perspective render to serve every elevation and material zone.
Lock footprint, massing, floor count, roof silhouette, bay and opening cadence, entrance position and material zoning.
Request rectified registration, neutral illumination and shadow-neutral surfaces where the role is a material or elevation source.
Forbid redesign, extra floors, invented wings, moved openings, baked entourage, directional sunlight and cast shadows.
Generate occupied depth as a separate clean layer for placement behind matching physical glazing.

provenance_contract.prompt_storage_rule: prompt_fields maps each semantic output role to the JSON field containing its complete, unmodified exact prompt; every mapped field must be retained in the same provenance record.
provenance_contract.retention_rule: Keep raw keeper outputs and the labelled goalpost under textures/source; a temporary download or conversation attachment is not an archival source.

pbr_derivation: Derive semantic near/far albedo, normal, roughness, AO, depth, emissive, glass and opaque channels from approved keeper sources.
Derive tile-safe construction zones from the same goalpost palette for long or nonlinear solids without replacing the registered identity source.
Register elevations and occupied-depth plates to audited datums and real openings while physical walls, recesses, panes, frames, screens, returns and roof junctions remain geometry.
Reject perspective, reflection or surrounding-object artifacts before a source can become a repeating construction material; use an orthographic shadow-neutral plate instead.
Preserve semantic zone names while deduplicating identical construction-image paths and using far LODs for secondary equipment.
keeper_loop: Render unchanged live cameras for front or street, corner, aerial or roof, and interior, courtyard or rear evidence as applicable.
Rank deltas in silhouette, opening cadence, material scale, glazing, construction depth and roof or corner continuity.
Correct the largest visible deltas, regenerate only the affected source or geometry and rerender the same cameras.
Promote a finite reviewed keeper batch and ship its comparison sheet before scaling another family.

always_model: entrance recess and canopy support logic
window recesses and stone returns at hero range
residential-scale sills, frames, curtain or privacy layers, eave junctions and occupied depth
deep monumental portal and lobby cavities with shaped soffits, jambs, panes and recessed occupation layers
every visible aisle, ridge, valley, clerestory and structural rib in a multi-aisle hall roof
cornice profiles and wrapping balcony slabs
bevels on exposed masonry, metal and timber edges
signature elements that alter silhouette or cast identity-defining shadows
visually open railings, pergolas and lightweight furniture as real posts, rails, balusters, beams, fins, seats, backs and legs
blend_rules: Never allow columns, pilasters or buttresses to cross window openings unless shown in the reference.
Every projection requires a believable attachment, return or support.
Use bevelled or profiled edges; avoid razor-sharp boxes on visible corners.
Place fixed corner geometry inside the module extent contract.
Weathering surfaces inherit the roof family; supports and fascias inherit facade masonry; frames and flashings inherit the building metal family.
Keep ceremonial entrances and landmark roof pavilions fixed in size while repeatable middle bays absorb footprint changes.
Reserve landmark bays before distributing repeatable dormers or windows so semantic assemblies never collide.
For wide landmark frontages preserve a fixed corner / secondary pavilion / centre pavilion / secondary pavilion / corner rhythm; only the bays between those anchors absorb width changes.
Continue every projected pavilion through the vertical LEGO stack and terminate it with a matching roof assembly; a facade projection without a skyline consequence reads as an applique.
Evaluate roof material inheritance from the City Prompt aerial camera as well as the hero view; horizontal roof surfaces hidden in a street render still dominate the Google Tiles scene.

Before export, compare exterior-skin, pane, room-card and structural-core planes on every facade axis; preserve a positive clearance behind the room card after all recess caps and coordinate transforms.

required_properties: separate podium, typical, alternate and crown bands
feature-registered UVs for every identity surface
generic tiling prohibited as the primary identity treatment
facade_pbr.delivery: KTX2/UASTC for close range, smaller compressed LOD for city scale

glazing.near: physical transmission, shape-matched recessed pane, semantic opening returns, slim registered mullions/transoms, projecting sill and occupied interior backplate
glazing.far: baked facade glass with semantic mask
glazing.occupancy_rule: Default visible windows to subtle warm occupied interiors; vary rooms or floors without creating a repeated cool/warm checkerboard.
glazing.materiality_rule: Choose a reference-specific optical profile for tint, roughness, coating, transmission and frame depth; the glass stays nearly non-emissive and room cards own interior warmth.
glazing.export_contract: Every physical pane exports glazing_profile, glazing_lod, environment intensity and cavity depth in glTF extras plus KHR clearcoat, transmission and specular material extensions; every City Prompt viewer preserves that profile. A proof renderer may temporarily disable transmission and lower alpha only after export, must restore the authored values, and may not change the delivery GLB.

lod.hero_strategy: physical glazing, full PBR atlas and semantic relief
lod.city_strategy: compressed baked facade, preserved silhouette and simplified interiors

batch_workflow.automation: Collect archetype, variant, all reference images, dimensions and footprint metadata; assign a confidence score.
batch_workflow.human_review: Only missing or contradictory reference sets.

batch_workflow.automation: Group entries by massing graph, architectural signature kits, material zones, roof family and glass profile.
Compile grammar, inject signature, check reference roles and footprint ranges without image API calls.
Generate or reuse rectified facade source, derive full PBR channels, semantic glass masks and LOD atlases.
batch_workflow.human_review: Only failed rectification, baked shadows, inconsistent floors or lost identity.

batch_workflow.automation: Build fixed semantic modules plus repeatable middle variants, wrap side elevations and export GLBs.
Validate origin, extents, stack, file integrity, quality-memory gates, shape matrix and LOD budgets.

Move the City Prompt camera through street/front, front-corner oblique, rear-corner oblique, high oblique/aerial and close-facade roles; generate camera-locked photoreal goal posts; compare the live model at the unchanged cameras plus a context view.
batch_workflow.human_review: Approve one representative per cluster, then spot-check confidence outliers.

batch_workflow.automation: Import only validation-pass and high-quality-ready manifests into City Prompt; retain provenance and memory version.

triangle_budget.policy: warn outside range; landmarks may exceed with explicit waiver

review_routing.pass: Eligible for automated City Prompt import after one cluster representative has visual approval.
review_routing.review: Continue the batch but add to the visual-review queue with failed gate reasons.
review_routing.fail: Do not import; retain logs and inputs for a resumable retry.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Boxy or cartoonish building
known_failure_patterns.cause: Generic rectangular massing with identity delegated to a flat image.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Add semantic massing, recesses, bevels, profiles and fixed signature assemblies.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A detailed LEGO family becomes a rectangular box when placed inside a four-vertex user polygon
known_failure_patterns.cause: The runtime treats the polygon as an extrusion mould and independently stretches every module or landmark axis to the parcel edges, erasing authored setbacks, shoulders, courts, chamfers, entrance recesses and roof volumes.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Treat the polygon as a site envelope. Require allow_inset_footprint on the authored modules, choose the fixed landmark only inside its audited band, and apply one common uniform horizontal contain scale to the complete landmark or stack so the archetype form remains centred inside the vertices.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Valid placed LEGO buildings persist as generic grey massing polygons in a mixed-family plan
known_failure_patterns.cause: The viewer caps detailed rendering by distinct-family count, so only the nearest few family asset sets mount while every later family is deliberately replaced by a massing proxy.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Admit every distinct family inside the supported total-stack budget and retain WebGL context recovery as the safety mechanism. Verify a mixed plan after assets settle: every saved LEGO recipe must display authored geometry and materials simultaneously.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Lifelike authored buildings are surrounded by pale blue, grey or white polygon boxes
known_failure_patterns.cause: The planning prism or outline is suppressed only after a transient GLB load event, while projected stencil side walls remain mounted for multi-building tile replacement and become visible as camera-facing wedges.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Suppress each planning solid and outline from the durable saved renderable recipe, then clip all supported disjoint footprints with one world-coordinate polygon-union shader mask and omit the projected stencil volumes whenever that mask is active.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A building is polished in one dimension but still falls below the Haussmann minimum standard
known_failure_patterns.cause: Shape, physical construction depth, photoreal material response and LEGO scalability were reviewed as independent optional features instead of one inseparable acceptance contract.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Record and prove all four pillars together in quality_standard_evidence: distinctive archetype-shaped masses, projecting/recessed/open construction, a human-approved render-locked PBR and glazing comparison, and fixed identity anchors plus complete repeatable middle roles across the declared shape matrix.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Roof windows look pasted on
known_failure_patterns.cause: Dormer material, depth and roof attachment do not match the roof system.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Integrate dormer cheeks and caps into the roof material and add occupied recessed glazing.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Cartoon ground floor
known_failure_patterns.cause: Flat doors, oversized frames, uniform glass and unsupported awning slabs.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Model recessed shopfront bays, transoms, kickplates, stone piers, dark timber/bronze doors and supported canopies only.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Dead dark-blue windows
known_failure_patterns.cause: Tinted alpha-blended planes without interiors or reflections.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Use physical transmission near and subtle warm occupied backplates; bake semantic glass far.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Windows are transparent but still look painted, frosted or checkerboard-like
known_failure_patterns.cause: One generic glass shader, emissive panes, whole-facade colour alternation or a rectangular backing card ignores the reference-specific sash and opening construction.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Author a family optical profile, keep glass nearly non-emissive, place varied occupation on recessed room cards, use coherent tint per sash and make multi-lite or curved openings real pane faces.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Front facade works but orbit view fails
known_failure_patterns.cause: Materials and architectural datums stop at the front edge.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Wrap materials, bands, returns and compatible detail around side elevations.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Detail collides with windows
known_failure_patterns.cause: Signature kits are placed on a generic spacing grid instead of the bay graph.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Derive every projection from semantic bay occupancy and test opening clearance.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Generated surface fights City Prompt lighting
known_failure_patterns.cause: Directional shadows and highlights are baked into albedo.
known_failure_patterns.correction: De-light albedo and keep lighting authority in the runtime environment.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: One rectangle looks good but user polygons fail
known_failure_patterns.cause: Corners and entrances were stretched with the middle facade.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Use fixed semantic end conditions and test every declared footprint profile at small and large dimensions.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A fixed landmark disappears when the user draws a slightly imperfect footprint
known_failure_patterns.cause: The planner requires exact native dimensions or applies an undocumented global stretch that can distort the one-off silhouette.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Declare and test a conservative per-family fixedLandmarkScaleBand with a bounded independent-axis ratio; retain the whole GLB for near-native drawings and switch oversized targets to the authored stack or streetwall fallback.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A showcase graph silently falls back to generic balcony modules
known_failure_patterns.cause: The authored reference dimensions or floor count do not match the pilot registry exactly.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Treat reference dimensions as an executable contract and preflight the selected width, depth and floors before rendering.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Physical curtain-wall grid looks like a second cage over the facade
known_failure_patterns.cause: Frame colour, bay count or datum does not match the rectified elevation.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Align physical mullions to the authored facade cadence, keep profiles shallow and use the archetype's metal finish rather than a universal black grid.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Landmark GLB has excessive materials despite using a small atlas set
known_failure_patterns.cause: Temporary per-elevation UV-bound shader clones survive into export.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Bake surface-specific bounds into vertex UVs, then remap clones to their canonical shared material before GLB export.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Generated source is beautiful but changes the archetype's storey count or massing
known_failure_patterns.cause: The image model optimized architectural plausibility without a strict elevation contract.
known_failure_patterns.correction: A/B providers only for failed sources, reject attractive but structurally unfaithful results, and preserve the accepted provider plus reference provenance in the cache.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Parallel 4K PBR derivation exhausts memory
known_failure_patterns.cause: Several full-resolution albedo, normal, roughness, AO and emissive arrays are resident simultaneously.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Limit PBR image derivation concurrency while allowing geometry compilation and lightweight validation to remain parallel.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Semantic window relief becomes oversized rectangles or a facade cage
known_failure_patterns.cause: A coarse or fallback glass mask was treated as precise opening geometry.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Use mask-only physical glazing until semantic regions are opening-accurate; add construction-scale relief from known bay datums rather than outlining uncertain mask groups.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Gothic, Romanesque or segmental windows acquire dark rectangular patches in close City Prompt views
known_failure_patterns.cause: The semantic glass schedule stored only rectangular bounding boxes, so the near facade cut-out, physical glass plane and room-card reveal ignored the authored arch silhouette.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Rasterize an audited shape-aware mask from the same registered boxes (pointed_arch, segmental_arch, round or polygon), rebuild every PBR LOD from that mask, and compare the same grazing camera before acceptance.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Chamfered corner is a blank wedge between otherwise finished elevations
known_failure_patterns.cause: Cardinal facade skins stop where the diagonal corner condition begins.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Author oriented facade skins for every visible chamfer, keep a fixed entrance corner, and validate both street diagonals plus the aerial view.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Historic landmark has detailed fronts but blank projecting sides
known_failure_patterns.cause: Tower and pavilion modules received front elevations without return-face material assignments.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Treat every projection as a small building: wrap both return faces, continue the roof junction, and validate orbit views before acceptance.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: European balconies look like black boxes attached to the facade
known_failure_patterns.cause: Solid end panels and unsupported slabs were used as shortcuts for open iron construction.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Use thin slabs, open end rails, regularly spaced pickets, small corbels and floor-datum alignment; never close an iron balcony with opaque end plates.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A high-quality facade becomes a flat hundred-metre wall when the user widens the parcel
known_failure_patterns.cause: The centre and corner identities were preserved but all intermediate frontage was treated as one repeat field.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Use a bounded five-part landmark rhythm with fixed secondary quarter pavilions, then distribute only ordinary bays inside the four remaining intervals.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: The street view is coherent but the tiles aerial shows a giant unrelated dark lid
known_failure_patterns.cause: A generic flat lead or membrane deck closed a heritage mansard above the visible eaves.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Close the roof with the archetype material and form—such as a verdigris hipped cap—and validate the entire upper plane from an oblique aerial camera.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: One generated family is selected for visually incompatible variants of the same catalogue archetype
known_failure_patterns.cause: Broad aliases used a parent ID even though variant reference sets encode different massing and stylistic identities.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Persist reference provenance at variant level, give each materially distinct variant its own family, and never broaden aliases merely to satisfy a stale selection ID.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A landmark facade repeats miniature towers or entrances across a user-sized frontage
known_failure_patterns.cause: The complete rectified elevation was registered with the default repeatable-bay span instead of its audited real-world building span.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Audit and persist the physical atlas span before PBR derivation; reserve complete elevations for fixed massing and repeat only explicitly cropped middle bays.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A pale sky or blank background is printed onto the top of a Gothic or monumental volume
known_failure_patterns.cause: Negative space around towers in a complete orthographic elevation was treated as opaque rectangular facade material.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Reject the generic stack and split the target into fixed tower/crown skins plus background-free repeatable wing or nave bands.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Photoreal brick or glass is crossed by pale rails, dark cages or mismatched columns
known_failure_patterns.cause: A generic geometry kit duplicated coursing, fins or piers already authored in the render-locked atlas, or assigned the wrong semantic material.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Let the audited atlas own micro-detail; add only shadow-casting depth, map each kit to the target material language and suppress geometry absent from the reference.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A heritage cornice becomes a blank full-height storey
known_failure_patterns.cause: The fixed crown inherited the typical floor height instead of its measured architectural height.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Store a variant-level crown height and assemble it independently from repeatable floors.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Mansard dormers read as blue boxes while the facade windows feel occupied
known_failure_patterns.cause: Generic physical glass was used in a deep historic roof opening without a room backplate.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Use recessed warm occupied interior cards for heritage dormers, with roof-matched cheeks, stone surrounds and lead or slate aprons.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: The generated model occupies only part of the drawn parcel
known_failure_patterns.cause: The assembly fell back to a catalogue suggested width and depth because footprint compatibility metadata was absent.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Always analyze the actual polygon, author a named native dimension tier when needed, and verify the selected plan's fit scale before placement.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Pale or empty wedges appear behind an otherwise correct model in Google Tiles
known_failure_patterns.cause: A projected stencil volume erased tile fragments that were behind the replacement in screen space but outside its geographic footprint.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Use true world-coordinate clipping for the single replacement footprint and do not mount the projected stencil volume at the same time.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A deleted 3D model cannot be rebuilt on its surviving planning polygon
known_failure_patterns.cause: A stale community compile marker or historical building ID still classified the zone as placed.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Treat the primary live building link as authoritative; an unlinked zone is ready to place and recipe saves must never target stale secondary IDs.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Front signs, entrances or fire escapes repeat around side and rear elevations
known_failure_patterns.cause: The principal elevation atlas and semantic mask were reused on every face.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Generate a clean secondary-elevation bay with its own semantic mask and physical repeat span, preserve it through PBR/LOD derivation, and register side/rear relief to that band.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Accurate windows acquire heavy black picture-frame outlines at close range
known_failure_patterns.cause: A complete physical perimeter frame was added over sash already present in the audited facade atlas.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Do not duplicate the outer perimeter. Let the atlas own its fine colour/weathering, but register slim physical mullions and transoms at the recessed pane plane so grazing views still have parallax and contact shadow.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Masonry window returns look like applied trim instead of wall depth
known_failure_patterns.cause: Return boxes were centred on the opening boundary, leaving half their width visible on the wall face.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Inset non-heritage jambs, head and sill wholly inside the semantic opening. Validate from head-on and grazing cameras in Google Tiles.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A high-quality facade contains blank gray or white vertical panels after LEGO resizing
known_failure_patterns.cause: The rectified source retained isolation-background margins or a fixed end insertion inside the repeatable middle crop.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Crop the elevation and semantic mask together to the building silhouette, then remove fixed end insertions from the middle-band source and model those insertions as fixed geometry.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A roof reads as generic blue slab, Quonset huts or floating black sticks
known_failure_patterns.cause: A signature barrel or glazed lantern was approximated with generic primitives and unconstrained roof equipment.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Suppress generic roof clutter and author the target section: shallow elliptical closed shells for barrel vaults, slope-registered ribs and ridge for glazed lanterns, and real columns, beams, timber slats and planters for occupied terraces.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Adding physical sash makes the textured facade disappear in the close City Prompt LOD
known_failure_patterns.cause: The runtime treated any near-only material, including a glazing frame, as proof that a complete replacement near facade sheet existed and hid the baked wall.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Detect replacement near facades by the near-sheet material identity or facade-sheet metadata only. Near-only frames, glass and interiors must not hide the baked facade when the city-detail asset has no complete near sheet.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A generated elevation becomes blank walls, doubled storeys or sky-colored crown panels in the modular model
known_failure_patterns.cause: Automatic semantic-mask or band detection merged glass with masonry/background, or sliced more than one architectural level into a repeatable module.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Store normalized opening_schedule.json and band_schedule.json beside the source. Rasterize exact rectangular, segmental or pointed openings and crop floor, alternate, crown, podium and side bands in both X and Y before PBR derivation. Replace singular chimney, tower or entrance pixels with fixed geometry.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Near-range windows turn into pale or white holes even though the far facade atlas is correct
known_failure_patterns.cause: The recessed pane or occupied room card crosses into a flush solid massing core, so the runtime reveals or transmits the core instead of the authored window assembly.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Inset or thin each structural core to create a continuous facade service cavity. Keep the stone face, return, pane, room card and core in strict depth order and validate the section in the live Google Tiles near LOD.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A requested sibling variant compiles with the geometry or image of the first variant
known_failure_patterns.cause: The export selected the variant description but retained the parent generationStyleInput and variant_0 image provenance.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Derive the selected variant index and rewrite archetypeId, archetypeLabel, archetypeImageUrl and archetypeImagePath before emitting the family source. Assert the exact UI generation id during validation.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A batch reports success but reuses an older GLB after Blender printed a Python traceback
known_failure_patterns.cause: Blender can exit with process code zero after an embedded Python exception, leaving stale output files available to downstream validation.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Treat Blender traceback and compiler error markers in stdout/stderr as hard failures, delete or version output directories per build, and validate manifest provenance against the requested family id.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: An octagonal lantern has detailed cardinal faces but blank diagonal wedges
known_failure_patterns.cause: The massing primitive became eight-sided while facade skins and physical window kits remained limited to front, rear, left and right axes.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Support oriented facade skins and construction-depth window arrays on arbitrary facade angles. Register every exposed polygon face and validate the lantern from aerial plus both diagonal street views.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A ceremonial entrance faces a railway, service lane or interior block instead of the public street
known_failure_patterns.cause: The family front axis was placed with the polygon's stored winding or a default zero rotation rather than an explicit public-frontage edge.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Persist frontage and service-edge semantics in the master-plan payload, derive rotation from the selected street edge, and include a live orientation gate before community acceptance.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Pale stone detail reads well offline but becomes flat white in Google Tiles
known_failure_patterns.cause: Bright runtime exposure, high-value albedo and insufficient mid-frequency normal/AO contrast compress the relief against sunlit photogrammetry.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Calibrate albedo values and PBR contrast in the live viewer, preserve shadow-neutral texture input, and validate the same model under sun-facing, backlit and grazing cameras before changing geometry.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A few hero buildings are convincing but a generated neighborhood is too heavy to orbit or capture as video
known_failure_patterns.cause: The close-range atlas, materials and construction geometry were delivered at one quality tier for every distance and every repeated instance.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Ship explicit hero, district and map LODs; instance shared modules/materials, compress textures with KTX2, preload route-visible assets and enforce district-wide triangle, texture and draw-call budgets.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Windows on a cylindrical turret look like blue decals or unrelated white boxes
known_failure_patterns.cause: The corner tower was fixed geometry but its windows were separate flat front-only curtain walls, so the openings did not follow both exposed tangent planes or the turret's masonry-band language.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Make the two outward tangent elevations part of the fixed turret assembly. Place recessed occupied panes just outside the opaque drum, use construction-depth stone returns, preserve the masonry course rhythm, and validate all four corners from street and aerial obliques.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Semantic graph windows ignore the selected glass profile and remain cool blue while facade-sheet glass is correct
known_failure_patterns.cause: Only masked facade-sheet overlay materials consumed the shared optical profile; generic graph glazing still used the catalogue fallback MAT_Glass values.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Build every unmasked semantic pane from the same profile-driven tint, roughness, transmission, IOR and clearcoat values, keep alpha opaque, and pair it with an always-lit occupied interior card.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A standalone replacement building sits inside a bright white or sky-coloured apron in Google Tiles
known_failure_patterns.cause: The spatial tile mask removes the source photogrammetry across the exact parcel, but an older/manual project has no separate compiled site-boundary surface to cover the cleared ground around an irregular model silhouette.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Mount a deterministic terrain-toned replacement surface under the clipped building footprint, add a small hidden overlap beneath surviving tiles to eliminate raster seams, and treat the entrance threshold and planting edge as the building-to-public-realm handoff.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A model matches the render's facade image but still feels flatter and less architectural than the render
known_failure_patterns.cause: The render carries sectional hierarchy beyond the atlas: deep traceried openings, sculpted arch profiles, roof cresting, projecting belts, steps and a landscaped threshold cast real silhouette and contact shadows.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Compare the live model and approved render at the same close camera. Promote every identity-bearing shadow line into fixed or repeatable construction geometry, then coordinate stairs, retaining edges, planting and furnishings through the public-realm LEGO recipe instead of painting them into the facade.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Windows and carved bays become unnaturally wide when a family is resized to the parcel
known_failure_patterns.cause: One complete facade photograph was UV-stretched across the target span even though it described a shorter authored bay period.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Record the real repeat period and tile only audited ordinary bays. Expand the facade skin, semantic openings, recessed glass and interiors with the identical repeat phase; keep podium, entrance, corners, crown and roof fixed.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A detailed Gothic facade is covered by pale external sticks or a rectangular scaffold
known_failure_patterns.cause: Unreviewed semantic-mask regions were promoted directly into jambs, sills, mullions or returns, and those shapes duplicated construction already visible in the atlas.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Reject broad or merged regions before geometry generation. Use an uncertain mask only for a recessed pane and occupied card; add slim physical returns or sash relief only after an audited opening schedule proves registration from head-on and grazing cameras.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Dark vertical slots remain between a textured wall and fixed cylindrical or polygonal corner towers
known_failure_patterns.cause: The repeatable wall skin stopped short of the corner assembly's inside tangent while the opaque service core remained visible through the gap.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Solve the exposed wall span from the fixed corner geometry. Extend the skin to overlap the inside tangent by a small construction tolerance, keep side spans independent from front spans, and verify every junction in an aerial orbit.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Stone courses, turret bands and eaves look like bright applied graphics in Google Tiles
known_failure_patterns.cause: Relief geometry duplicated atlas bands with excessive projection, thickness or albedo contrast, so it separated visually from the wall material language.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Let the atlas own fine coursing. Use shallow construction-scale relief only for shadow-bearing datums, inherit the same warm stone PBR family, reduce exposed profile, and calibrate in live photogrammetry rather than compensating with brighter materials.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A multi-peak tensile roof reads as a faceted mountain range with hard ridges between peaks
known_failure_patterns.cause: Independent roof primitives or a maximum-of-peaks height field created discontinuous transitions instead of a shared cable-net surface.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Build one continuous roof mesh tied to the envelope edge, blend peak influence with a smooth high-order norm, retain real saddle valleys and validate the complete seam network from an oblique aerial view.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A large reflective glass landmark becomes milky white or uniformly dead blue
known_failure_patterns.cause: A clear window-glass profile was stretched across the full envelope without reflection density or occupied-zone variation.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Use a darker physical reflective-skin material for the continuous envelope, preserve warm occupied lower foyer zones, and keep entrance and aperture glazing as separate clear construction assemblies.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A free-form landmark has plausible geometry but still reads like a procedural grey model
known_failure_patterns.cause: Flat catalogue materials or one complete elevation image were expected to describe several unrelated systems: historic brick, warped curtain wall and a metallic tensile roof.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Generate and retain separate shadow-neutral PBR sources for each continuous material system. Register repeatable warehouse brick only to exposed masonry skins, curtain-wall panels only to the warped envelope, and top-down metallic cladding only to the roof; keep silhouette and openings in geometry.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A realistic curtain-wall atlas fights the physical mullions, tiles at the perimeter seam or makes Blender's joined bevel take minutes
known_failure_patterns.cause: The image period did not match the panel cadence, or a multi-repeat authored unwrap was applied before the global joined-mesh bevel.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Match atlas columns and rows to physical mullion/transom counts, correct the cyclic seam per polygon and apply the registered shell UVs after beveling. Keep aperture and entrance glazing on independent materials so the envelope atlas cannot leak into those assemblies.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: An image-to-3D landmark looks excellent in one GLB but cannot be resized, restacked or safely imported as a LEGO family
known_failure_patterns.cause: The generator fused roof, facade, apertures, entrance and base into one high-triangle mesh with one baked material and no semantic module boundaries.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Preserve the original GLB with Git LFS, record its hash, normalize it to the authored metric envelope, crop and decimate only the identity-bearing crown/roof above a documented interface, and classify it as a non-repeatable fixed assembly. Rebuild the ordinary base from registered repeatable bays and validate the combined manifest as a fixed landmark plus parametric fallback family.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A strong image-to-3D silhouette still carries a blurry city panorama, black reflection band or one material across glass, roof and historic masonry
known_failure_patterns.cause: The fused source retained its single baked scene material after cropping, so unrelated construction systems shared one UV/photo treatment and identity openings remained only texture artifacts.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Classify retained faces into semantic glass, roof and transition regions; assign each region a registered PBR source with its own projection; and rebuild apertures and the public entrance as independent depth assemblies while preserving the original fixed mesh and source hash.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A valid cultural or industrial catalogue entry fails grammar compilation because its storeys exceed six metres
known_failure_patterns.cause: Residential floor-height limits were applied universally to acoustic halls and large assembly spaces.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Permit a reviewed non-residential floor-height range, preserve catalogue provenance and add a regression test using the canonical tall-storey entry.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A theater passes a shape-count gate but repeats its marquee or entrance around L, U or courtyard footprints
known_failure_patterns.cause: The manifest padded preferredProfiles with shapes that contradict a single-frontage auditorium solely to satisfy a global minimum.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Declare the honest rectangle profile, set an explicit minimumPreferredProfiles exception with profileRationale, and prove clean in-band assembly plus oversized streetwall_repeat behavior.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A selected catalogue variant imports correctly but planner cards resolve to a generic or incompatible family
known_failure_patterns.cause: The generated manifest omitted either the parent archetype id or selected variant id from archetype_aliases.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Emit both identities as explicit aliases, retain the source variant id, and regression-test the imported planner metadata.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A stacked theater grows repeated blade signs, marquees or fly towers on ordinary floors
known_failure_patterns.cause: Fixed civic identity assemblies were authored inside a repeatable middle-floor kit.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Keep marquee, portal and blade sign in the podium; keep the fly tower in the roof or crown; repeat only the ordinary occupied wall rhythm.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A civic archetype has detailed textures but still reads as a generic rectangular office block
known_failure_patterns.cause: Every vertical module filled the complete nominal parcel envelope, erasing the shallow lobby, deeper hall, stepped shoulders, roof volume and service tower visible in the reference.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Treat native dimensions as the matching envelope. Construct role-specific occupied solids inside it, allow inset module extents, and validate the assembled silhouette against front, rear-corner and aerial reference views.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: An arena, dome or inhabited-arch landmark is technically modular but still reads as a box, or its exported bounds no longer match the authored envelope
known_failure_patterns.cause: The one-off silhouette was forced into ordinary stacked rectangular roles, or an imported image-to-3D hierarchy was compressed/exported without freezing world transforms and validating the delivered GLB.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Ship the canonical form as a variant-bound fixed assembled landmark with physical ellipse, dome, arch, portico, oculus and cable-net geometry. Keep a separate conservative six-module fallback for oversized streetwall-repeat planning, freeze imported hierarchies in world space, normalize the metric envelope and validate final on-disk bounds.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A curved landmark matches in 3D dimensions but its roof edge, entrance crests, material bands or media ribbon still miss the camera-locked archetype by visible screen-space offsets
known_failure_patterns.cause: The iteration compared only world dimensions; perspective and shell depth moved supposedly aligned facade features to different image rows.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Register silhouette top and base, roof edge, oculus extents, band boundaries, entrance crests and ribbons in the locked hero camera. Adjust continuous shell-following profiles against those landmarks, then confirm the correction remains plausible in front-corner, rear-corner and aerial views.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A monumental arena entrance staircase reads as another window or as a ramp tacked onto the facade
known_failure_patterns.cause: The portal remained a material-swapped facade panel, or the stairs were built as a bright solid wedge projecting outside the shell instead of circulation carved through it.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Delete the exterior and concourse faces inside the portal, clip crossing facade structure, place the first riser at the shell plane, climb inward with distinct tread or escalator runs, and terminate at a recessed occupied landing framed by shell-derived cheeks, soffit and handrails.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A building declares complete PBR channels but still looks generic, smooth or unrelated to its archetype photos
known_failure_patterns.cause: A generic material tile or broad style atlas was repeated across the model; the reference-specific elevation was never registered to semantic surfaces, and the declared depth map was not connected to the runtime shader.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Generate or derive a render-locked source from the exact compatible archetype views, register shared coordinates across each identity surface, bind normal plus depth/displacement in the shader, retain physical shadow-casting geometry, and fail review whenever generic_tiling_allowed is not explicitly false.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A monumental glass lobby or station portal reads as a flat orange window instead of a carved public interior
known_failure_patterns.cause: One uniformly bright emissive backplate filled the entire opening, eliminating the depth hierarchy between exterior pane, structure, occupied rooms and dark void.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Build a shaped cavity with deep jambs and soffit, physical mullions and panes, a dark recessed backplane, and only sparse warm ceiling bands or room cards. Verify portal depth in facade-close and front-corner views.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A market or station looks convincing from the front but its aerial view collapses into one generic roof shell
known_failure_patterns.cause: The generator modeled only the outer roof envelope and omitted the repeated aisles, ridges, valleys, clerestories, ribs, purlins and end fans that define the reference engineering system.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Author each roof aisle or vault as a complete structural bay, continue its ribs and glazing across the full depth, expose valleys and clerestories, and validate both aerial and rear-corner renders.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: An engineered market roof has the right truss count but reads as a generic transparent greenhouse in aerial and oblique views
known_failure_patterns.cause: The model assigned glazing to every sloped roof field even though the compatible references separate opaque zinc or tile weathering planes from narrow transparent ridge lanterns.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Map roof material hierarchy from the aerial evidence before detailing: build opaque weathering fields, terracotta or flashing bands and transparent clerestories as separate geometry, then verify opacity, ridge count and valley continuity from high oblique and roof-plan views.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A sculptural concert hall resembles its card image from the front but becomes stacked ribbons, an open-backed stage set or a black canopy from other angles
known_failure_patterns.cause: The free-form envelope was assembled from disconnected hero-facing strips, or the same exterior material and normals were used for both sunlit shell tops and deeply shaded undersides.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Infer a compatible front, rear, side and aerial envelope from every available reference, build continuous closed shell loops around the plan, and assign fascia and underside or acoustic soffit as explicit semantic surfaces. Validate the hero camera only after rear-corner and aerial silhouette continuity is proven.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A fallback LEGO module exports below ground after adding an arched opening
known_failure_patterns.cause: A semicircular arch was sized wider than twice the usable module height, so the spring line and lower curve could not fit inside the module envelope.
known_failure_patterns.correction: For semicircular fallback arches keep opening width at or below twice the usable module height; otherwise use a shallower segmental arch or move the identity-bearing opening into the fixed assembled landmark. Validate on-disk module bounds.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A reference-locked front facade is convincing but its long secondary elevations read as smooth slabs, enlarged brick mosaics or stretched front windows
known_failure_patterns.cause: The ceremonial front atlas or one narrow crop was stretched across a wall with a different aspect ratio and opening rhythm, while bright physical bands were applied over the result.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Author a dedicated true-aspect secondary-elevation PBR source at real masonry course scale, register its own opening schedule and alpha voids, and use physical geometry only for construction-depth returns, sills and sashes. Validate brick scale and course continuity in a front-corner oblique.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A hipped roof with a flat service zone reads as a dark slab floating above the corrugation or as a wire lattice crossing skylights
known_failure_patterns.cause: A complete hip remained beneath a second deck mesh, and physical standing seams continued through the deck, crossed other roof faces or converged repeatedly at one corner.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Build the perimeter hip from an explicit inner contour that meets the service deck at one shared elevation. Terminate seams at the inner edge and skylight curbs, distribute necessary ribs without corner clamping, and let registered normal/depth relief carry directions that would otherwise cross. Prove the topology from street-corner and aerial views.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A standard-building stoop entrance or courtyard passage still reads as another window, a painted dark rectangle or an object tacked onto the facade
known_failure_patterns.cause: The full podium core and registered facade card remained behind the opening while stairs, an arch frame or a passage lining were added only in front.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Treat the feature as a subtractive fixed podium assembly: split or cut the envelope and front/rear skin, preserve the full circulation path, begin stairs at the facade plane, and terminate them at a recessed door or occupied landing framed by real jambs, soffit or ceiling and threshold geometry.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A residential balcony stack looks like repeated opaque boxes or shows ghost balconies behind the modeled rails
known_failure_patterns.cause: An emissive pane was mistaken for an occupied room, or the reference elevation already contained rendered balconies that were duplicated by misaligned physical slabs and railings.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Use a clean reference-palette wall PBR beneath the stack, recess a darker layered door or room card, and construct each balcony once with a thin slab, timber or masonry returns, open end rails, regularly spaced pickets and consistent floor-datum anchoring.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A monumental atrium looks acceptable head-on but becomes an open glass card with exposed floor plates or an opaque rooftop box in oblique views
known_failure_patterns.cause: Only the front curtain wall was constructed, while return facets and the glass roof were omitted or occupied backplates extended beyond the glazing envelope.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Build front, both faceted returns and roof as one closed transparent section; keep every plate, brace and occupied room card inside those boundaries; and validate front-corner plus aerial views before accepting the optical profile.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A family ships a custom elevation and complete PBR package but its windows and facade still look generic in the delivered GLB
known_failure_patterns.cause: The render-locked source was declared in metadata but no exported material consumed it, while physical glass looked onto a uniform room card and discarded the reference-specific floor, bay and occupation cadence.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Audit the GLB material graph, not only the source folder. Bind the exterior source to its authored semantic surfaces and coordinate-register a reference-derived occupied-depth underlay behind the matching physical glazing; keep fins, mullions and other screens in separate geometry and prove the registration from front and oblique cameras.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A crystalline civic facade reads as an oversized triangular quilt or a generic honeycomb unrelated to the reference enclosure
known_failure_patterns.cause: A rectangular curtain-wall grid was split decoratively, or one uniform hexagon was repeated without using the documented panel count, clipped shape families, material ratio and curved opening boundary.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Reconstruct a wrapped unitized panel topology at evidence-based scale; mix the authored four-, five- and six-sided families, preserve the opaque-to-glazed schedule, clip panels to subtractive openings, and keep pressure-cap seams visible between every neighbouring unit.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A curved shell, long timber member or deep stone arcade shows stretched windows, baked shadows or giant facade fragments even though a custom elevation exists
known_failure_patterns.cause: The complete render-locked elevation was reused as a generic tiling material on nonlinear or elongated construction surfaces instead of remaining a coordinate-registered identity source.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Separate reference registration from construction materialization. Use tile-safe shadow-neutral shell, timber, stone and dome zones derived from the goalpost palette on physical solids; keep silhouette openings in geometry; and clip the reference-derived occupied-depth plate to each matching real pane or arch.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A detached house has plausible wall materials but still reads as a generic miniature apartment block or loses its identity when the user draws a slightly different footprint
known_failure_patterns.cause: The generator treated the house as interchangeable stacked boxes, reduced the roof and threshold to caps, or stretched individual windows, porches, screens and balconies instead of preserving their composition.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Author a fixed whole-house landmark whose roof silhouette, entrance, porch or balcony, privacy screen, chimney or tower and residential window cavities form one reviewed composition. Permit bounded whole-building scaling, then route larger targets to a fallback kit that repeats complete residential bays while keeping the entrance, ends and roof fixed.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A detailed detached-house screen fuses into a pale solid wall, or exposed historic masonry reads as brick stickers applied over clean stucco
known_failure_patterns.cause: Fine battens were sized without proving screen-space gaps and recessed occupation in the locked corner camera, while regular brick grids were projected proud of the finish without a mortar recess or chipped plaster boundary.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Calibrate batten width, spacing, projection and a meaningful air gap against the corner view; recess glass and varied dark occupied rooms behind it. Treat exposed masonry as loss of finish: keep brick nearly flush or recessed over a shadowed mortar bed and author ragged, irregular plaster edges.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A later family regresses to generic skins because an earlier successful image-generation method cannot be reproduced
known_failure_patterns.cause: The exact prompt, compatible inputs, provider and model, keeper role or registered surfaces existed only in chat history, temporary downloads or an unlabelled beauty render.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Archive the labelled goalpost and immutable semantic keeper sources under textures/source, record exact prompts and required provenance in reference-generation.json, derive registered near/far PBR and occupied-depth channels, and ship the locked-camera comparison sheet with the family.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A courtyard ring roof has the right four strips in plan but reads as crossed gables, triangular fins or smooth pyramids at its corners
known_failure_patterns.cause: Independent gabled strips retained their end-cap faces inside perpendicular intersections, while diagonal beams or unregistered corner fillers were mistaken for one connected roof topology.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Stop each straight roof at the corner bay, remove internal gable end caps and bridge every junction with a four-plane hip sharing the strip ridge and eave elevations. Model the inner valley and exterior hip lines separately, apply true-scale roof UVs to the corner planes, and prove the uninterrupted open void from street-corner and aerial cameras.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A custom-skinned rear wall, pergola or railing shows warped buildings, reflections or furniture printed across its surface
known_failure_patterns.cause: An oblique reference photograph was cropped and repeated as a construction material instead of being limited to a registered view-dependent source.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Replace the repeating crop with an orthographic shadow-neutral construction plate derived from the same reference palette. Keep perspective evidence on coordinate-registered elevation or occupied-depth cards, and rebuild visually open railings and pergolas as real members.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A high-quality custom-skinned GLB becomes too large for reliable mobile loading even though many material zones share the same brick, metal or timber source
known_failure_patterns.cause: Every semantic zone embedded a separate copy of identical high-resolution image channels and secondary equipment consumed hero-range atlases.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Keep distinct semantic materials and complete near/far source packages, but point related exported materials at the same approved construction-image paths and use far LODs for secondary equipment. Verify the delivered GLB still retains required custom textures and optical metadata.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A procedural roof or truss renders correctly but the exported GLB reports an impossible vertical extent equal to one long beam length
known_failure_patterns.cause: The final generated cylinder received a quaternion and was immediately composed into a rotated wing through its still-stale matrix_world; creating the next object had incidentally flushed every earlier member.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Flush Blender's view-layer dependency graph after assigning procedural member quaternions and before composing parent or wing transforms. Apply the intended origin offset to physical gutters and caps, then validate the final on-disk GLB bounds rather than trusting the Blender render.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A segmental or semicircular window has the correct outline but its visible head reads as a staircase in the close render
known_failure_patterns.cause: The curved frame or spandrel was assembled from many separate beam chords or vertical filler strips, so every joint caught its own highlight.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Build the spandrel as one continuous face and the visible arch frame as one continuous ribbon with sufficient curve segments for the locked close camera. Keep jambs, threshold, mullions and recessed glazing independent.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A custom-skinned office or laboratory curtain wall still reads as one dark repeated image rather than transparent glass with occupied depth
known_failure_patterns.cause: The outer glass albedo baked reflections, mullions and an interior scene while a second occupied card repeated behind it, merging both optical layers into a dense texture.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Retain the approved glass source for roughness, normal and restrained reflection variation, wash its base colour toward the registered neutral tint, and place a separately registered warm occupied-depth source behind each physical pane. Keep pressure caps, spandrels and slabs as geometry.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A fixed landmark fits its documented shaft height but the mast, roof lantern, photovoltaic rack or screen clips the camera or exceeds the manifest envelope
known_failure_patterns.cause: Native dimensions were recorded before identity-bearing roof and crown assemblies were included in the delivered bounds.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Compute the complete assembled bounds after every crown and roof element is built, store that full metric height in the manifest and design lock, and prove the entire extent in hero, elevation and aerial renders.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A dense physical curtain wall takes many minutes to regenerate even though its panes, caps and slab edges are simple cuboids
known_failure_patterns.cause: Every repeated primitive invoked context-dependent Blender operators and transform application, making tooling overhead dominate visual iteration.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Create the metric vertices, faces, material slot and UVs directly for repeated simple meshes. Preserve bevels, semantic extras and separate optical layers, then verify that the optimized generator exports the same physical facade and close-view result.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A planted tower has real planters and trunks but still reads as sparse plastic landscaping or turns into dark rectangular cards in the exported GLB
known_failure_patterns.cause: Foliage identity was reduced to low-poly spheres, or chroma-key crown cards relied on viewport alpha without an explicit transparent shader, blend mode and multi-camera proof.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Combine real soil, planter, trunk and branching skeleton geometry with a labelled photoreal foliage cutout. Drive transparency through an explicit alpha mix shader and glTF blend mode, use only crossed vertical crown planes, and verify street, corner, aerial and mobile views for black quads or grazing horizontal cards.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A gateway, arcade or entrance looks dark and recessed from the front but remains a solid wall in plan or cannot show the court beyond
known_failure_patterns.cause: A tunnel-coloured box and portal frame were placed in front of one unbroken mass instead of splitting the building envelope around a continuous circulation void.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Split every intersecting mass, facade skin and floor strip around the full passage. Model only jambs, spandrels, ceiling ribs, returns, paving and folded doors, then prove an uninterrupted sightline and walking volume from both sides.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A cable-stayed canopy contains a mast, cables and branching columns but they read as decorative lines floating near a glass box
known_failure_patterns.cause: Trunks were buried behind the curtain wall, branches missed the roof nodes, stay endpoints used a different roof equation, or the mast stopped at an unrelated slab.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Author one load-path function shared by roof nodes, tree-column branches and stay endpoints. Keep primary trunks outside the glazing, connect every branch and cable to visible canopy nodes, carry the mast to a credible base, and prove the network in front elevation, roof aerial and structural close views.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A tall wall, tower pier or long roof member displays giant masonry blocks or stretched construction imagery even though the source texture is tile-safe
known_failure_patterns.cause: One normalized UV island was stretched across the full physical object while repeated instances shared a unit mesh that ignored architectural texture scale.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Preserve true construction scale by splitting identity-bearing masses into coursed lifts or by assigning physical-scale coordinates before export. Keep shared metric mesh instances for genuinely repeated parts, and reject any hero or close view where the material scale changes with object dimensions.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Several unrelated new families are detailed and textured but still read as the same generic box with different colours
known_failure_patterns.cause: One universal bay scaffold was reused before identifying each archetype's structural and enclosure grammar, so setbacks, gable load paths, freestanding frames, transparent concourses and deep rainscreens became surface decoration.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Select a family-specific structural grammar from the multi-angle goalpost before building bays. Construct its continuous primary load path and enclosure first, then author compatible repeatable semantic bays rather than forcing the family through a generic facade template.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A gabled or environmental roof matches from one street angle but its ridge runs the wrong direction, or its photovoltaic and sedum fields disappear in the aerial render
