known_failure_patterns.cause: Roof orientation was inferred from the hero alone, or finish planes were coplanar with and quantized beneath their carrier surface during glTF export.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Lock ridge, eaves, slopes and field coverage against front plus aerial goalposts before detailing. Build PV, sedum, tile and rooflight fields as separate physical assemblies and keep them clearly proud of the carrier plane to survive export quantisation.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A machiya lattice, transit louver or passive-house blind reads as a dark printed panel instead of an open shading or privacy layer
known_failure_patterns.cause: The screen was baked into an opaque facade, fused to the pane, or packed so densely that its gaps and air cavity vanished at the locked camera.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Model each screen as real members with audited screen-space gaps, preserve an air cavity, and place reference-specific physical glazing plus occupied depth behind it. Prove the layer order in a grazing facade close view.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Photovoltaics, planted roofs or rooflights appear as decorative stickers that do not follow the roof construction or survive modular assembly
known_failure_patterns.cause: Environmental systems were treated as texture motifs without true coverage, supports, edge clearances, drainage relationships or a fixed roof-module contract.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Construct each environmental system at metric scale with separate carrier, support or frame geometry and roof-edge clearance. Preserve the system in the fixed assembled landmark and the semantic crown or roof module, then compare street and aerial proofs.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A transparent pavilion looks like a stack of cubicles or floating posters even though its glass shader is physically transparent
known_failure_patterns.cause: The same opaque occupied-depth image was placed close behind every pane, breaking one open gallery into repeated two-dimensional room cards.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Remove per-pane occupation cards. Continue floor and ceiling returns into one coherent interior, model sparse partitions, furniture and lights at real depth, and let the physical low-iron glass reveal that shared volume.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A passive-house facade repeats the same bright living-room photograph in every window and its blinds appear tacked onto shallow glazing
known_failure_patterns.cause: Occupied-depth imagery was uniform and too close to the pane, while the pane, insulated returns and blind hardware were not authored as a layered wall section.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Recess split low-E panes behind complete jamb, head and sill returns; place real blind blades, headbox and guides in front; then vary deep room shadow, selective occupied depth and physical curtain layers behind the glass.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A solar roof reads as one stretched blue sheet or its cell pattern changes scale with the building
known_failure_patterns.cause: One photovoltaic image was mapped across the whole roof field instead of being registered once per standard module with physical racking.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Build individual framed modules at true metric scale, map one complete countable cell topology to each module, preserve real gaps and mounting rails, and prove the array in an aerial close view.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: Two catalogue sibling variants load as the same building with different colours or one variant silently falls back to the parent family
known_failure_patterns.cause: The sibling reused the parent's goalpost, geometry, signature or assembled GLB, or its variant and aesthetic aliases were omitted during import and matching.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Treat the sibling as an independent family: lock its own compatible multi-angle source board, build its distinct massing, entrance, roof, glazing and materials, export a variant-tagged fixed landmark plus semantic fallback modules, and test every declared alias through the planner.

known_failure_patterns.symptom: A civic or industrial landmark contains the right ski path, roof ribs, conveyor gallery, market vault or entrance stair as isolated motifs but the building still looks toy-like and cannot plausibly function
known_failure_patterns.cause: Program-defining circulation, structure or process equipment was modeled as decorative fragments without continuous geometry, credible supports, landings, clearances or connections to occupied space.
known_failure_patterns.correction: Trace the complete route or load path from start to finish before adding surface detail. Join every segment to its architectural endpoint, model supports and guards at metric scale, preserve the connected system in the assembled GLB, and prove continuity in front, oblique and aerial comparisons.
